slides.title: Cell-state markers must be compared with actual behavior
body: The young-donor study identified inflammatory microglial states and altered interactions with vascular cells after repeated impacts. Such molecular states describe which genes were active in the sampled nuclei. They do not directly show how each living cell surveyed tissue or responded to a damaged synapse.

Functional comparisons require a preparation in which the relevant cells can be observed over time. Cell movement, contact duration, and collection of material are separate actions that can be quantified. The human tissue observations identify which populations and states should be examined in those assays.

The accompanying three-dimensional human model recording follows microglia actively surveying their environment. Its moving processes provide a direct behavioral readout of the cell. The model does not replace the human CTE dataset; it supplies an experimentally accessible function that can be compared with a disease-associated molecular state.

slides.title: Prevention targets exposure before a lesion is established
body: Reducing repeated head-impact exposure acts earlier in the biological sequence than attempting to remove established tau filaments. Rules, practice design, contact opportunities, and appropriate concussion management can alter the circumstances in which injury occurs. Their effects should be measured through actual exposure and health outcomes.

A helmet can reduce some injury risks without eliminating brain acceleration or establishing complete protection from CTE. Acute symptom recovery also does not directly report the long-term fate of tau or vulnerable cell populations. These outcomes occur at different stages and require different measurements.

There is no established disease-modifying cure that reverses confirmed CTE pathology. Care during life addresses the person's actual symptoms and other treatable contributors, while mechanism research tests specific cellular targets. Reducing exposure, managing acute injury, and investigating chronic pathology are distinct interventions within the same biological sequence.

slides.title: Culture architecture changes the network readout
body: The human model investigators compared three-dimensional tissue with a two-dimensional coculture. Both preparations showed spontaneous calcium activity, but the two-dimensional recording lacked the same network synchronization. A difference in tissue organization therefore changed the functional pattern even before assigning a disease effect.

The original comparison recording follows this two-dimensional activity. The cells are active, so absence of synchrony does not mean that every neuron has stopped functioning. It identifies a particular network property that depends on the preparation and must be considered when interpreting a perturbation.

The three-dimensional platform also maintained incorporated microglia for extended periods and supported interactions among neurons and astrocytes. These demonstrated properties permit controlled tests of multicellular mechanisms. A CTE application would still need disease-relevant tau, exposure conditions, and comparison with the specific human lesion or cell state being investigated.

items.text: Diagnosis requires the characteristic neuronal phosphorylated-tau lesion around small vessels at cortical sulcal depths; symptoms and photographs cannot establish it in a living player.
Football includes diagnosed concussions and repeated impacts without recognized symptoms. Exposure estimates and selected brain donations do not directly establish population prevalence.

items.lead: Axons and tau have normal functions.
items.text: Spectrin, actin, microtubules, and tau support axonal mechanics, transport, and synaptic organization. Pathological modification and assembly can disturb these functions.

items.lead: CTE involves more than tau deposits.
items.text: Human studies identify selective neuronal loss, white-matter changes, vascular responses, and altered immune-cell states. These measurements test different aspects of neuronal survival and tissue function.
Cell cultures, worms, fish, mice, and human tissue preparations isolate mechanisms. A model of seeding, clearance, or injury is not automatically a model that reproduces CTE.

items.lead: Clinical evidence must match the claim.
items.text: Current biomarkers can reflect other pathology, including Alzheimer disease. Exposure reduction, concussion care, and treatment of symptoms remain important while CTE-specific diagnostics and therapies are investigated.
